correctness.rationale: The fixed geometric support of a simplicial action is a union of complete vertex orbits with equal barycentric weights. Rotations r^t first compress the original cycle to C_t^k; if t<=k a nontrivial rotational orbit is internally adjacent and there is no nonempty fixed simplex. For t>k, the two normalized reflection axes have exactly the listed permissible orbit indices V0 and V1; computing direct and reflected circular distances between two permissible pairs shows the latter are >k and conflicts occur precisely for index difference <=k. Endpoint singleton cases obey the same rule. Thus fixed locus is PL the independence complex of an induced k-th path-power, an interval graph; the cited chordal simplicial-vertex splitting yields the stated finite wedge recursion with B_empty=z^-1, isolated-vertex case zero. This proves the complete all-n,k,H statement and its empty and S0 boundaries. Independently constructed orbit graphs agreed in 1,147 distinct small graph/group instances (4<=n<=18, k<=5; all t|n, reflection parameters), not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The elementary fixed-support orbit argument and chordal graph sphere-wedge splitting are previous tools. The contribution that survives comparison is the explicit simultaneous dihedral reflection-subgroup orbit conflict graph being an induced path-power, with all fixed-space PL types, exact Betti recursion, and mixed-dimensional C22^3 example. Neither ordinary cycle-power splittings nor broad chordal wedge theorems implies that a reflection orbit graph is chordal. No found stronger published theorem supplies these exact models; this is a bounded priority judgment, not proof of universal absence.

value.rationale: A group-equivariant fixed-locus identification for an entire two-parameter family of natural flag complexes supplies usable exact integral homology and homotopy data for all reflection subgroups. Its mixed-dimensional case shows a distinction from previously obtained single-sphere fixed loci. The complete induced interval-model and terminating recursion are structural, not mere parameter substitution or an isolated test.
